measures: Whether the resume evidences working fluently with AI coding tools as a practice -- what the candidate does differently because of them, not that they have heard of them.
source: Criteria drafted for ticket 11 against the category 04 defined and the 3/6 evidence 02 recorded (inventory.md, 'What the taxonomy cannot see', item 3: amex, fluidstack, ramp). Written first of the three because rule_share is 0 -- criterion agreement is the only agreement this category has.

criteria.name: named tooling
criteria.question: Does any bullet name a specific AI coding tool, assistant or agentic development workflow?
criteria.yes_requires: A quote naming the tool -- Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, an agentic coding workflow. A named product or a named practice both count; a category noun on its own does not.
criteria.no_looks_like: 'Familiar with modern AI tooling', 'used LLMs day to day', 'AI-first engineer' -- nothing a reader could go and look up.

criteria.name: the candidate's own work
criteria.question: Is the tooling used on the candidate's own engineering work, rather than being a product they built, sold or advised on?
criteria.yes_requires: The bullet that names the tool describes the candidate writing, reviewing, testing, debugging or refactoring code with it.
criteria.no_looks_like: 'Built an agent on the OpenAI Agents SDK', 'advised customers on Claude Code rollouts' -- real work, and it is Agentic systems or a consulting bullet, not this category.

criteria.name: changed practice
criteria.question: Does a bullet say what the tooling changed about how the work is done?
criteria.yes_requires: A stated difference -- what the candidate now does that they did not before, or stopped doing: a review step added, a class of work taken on, a cycle shortened, a task moved from hand-written to generated-and-verified.
criteria.no_looks_like: The tool is named and nothing follows. 'Used Cursor daily', 'Claude Code power user', a tool sitting in the skills list.

criteria.name: the change is checkable
criteria.question: Is that change stated as a fact somebody could check -- a number, a duration, a rate, a before and after?
criteria.yes_requires: A quantity attached to the change: PRs per week, hours to a first draft, a review-cycle time, a share of a codebase, a migration size.
criteria.no_looks_like: 'Dramatically faster', 'significantly more productive', '10x engineer' -- an adverb where the number goes.

criteria.name: past their own keyboard
criteria.question: Does the resume say the practice reached past the candidate's own editor -- other people, a standard, or a guardrail?
criteria.yes_requires: Team adoption, a written guideline, a review or eval standard for generated code, a tool or harness they built for others, teaching or onboarding.
criteria.no_looks_like: Every mention is first-person solo use; nothing says anyone else's work changed. A tool the candidate built and sold or shipped to others is a product, not their practice spreading -- C2 has already answered no in that case, and so does this one.

bands.label: E
bands.name: No tooling named
bands.reads: Nothing in the resume names an AI coding tool or an agentic development practice.

bands.label: D
bands.name: Named, not practised
bands.rule: C1 met, and either C2 or C3 unmet
bands.reads: A tool is named, but it is somebody else's product, or nothing says what it changed about the work.

bands.label: C
bands.name: A practice, described
bands.rule: C1, C2 and C3 met, neither C4 nor C5
bands.reads: The candidate says what the tooling changed about their own work, and asks the reader to take it on trust.

bands.label: B
bands.name: A practice, evidenced
bands.rule: C1, C2 and C3 met, and exactly one of C4, C5
bands.reads: The change is either measured or visible in someone else's work -- one of the two.

bands.label: A
bands.name: Fluent, and it shows
bands.reads: A named tool changed named work by a checkable amount, and the practice reached past this one person.
